Who We Are

At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years.

What We Do

The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride!

Role Overview

The International team is seeking a talented and driven Software Engineer II to join CarGurus' first engineering team in Ireland and work on exciting product initiatives for our Canadian and UK markets. In this role, you’ll be responsible for the full software development lifecycle – across both the frontend and backend – collaborating with Engineering and Product peers to design innovative solutions and tackle complex challenges for our dealer-facing products.

Building new, full-stack features for dealer products from the ground up
Integrating with existing services and expanding functionality using React, TypeScript, and Java

Collaborate with engineers and product managers across the organization to understand and solve new product requirements and tackle technical challenges.
Work with Java, Spring Boot, React, JavaScript/TypeScript, AWS, and other modern technologies to build consumer and dealer products.
Collaborate on system design and write well-crafted code to help evolve our service-oriented architecture.
Be deeply engaged in the full development lifecycle: designing, developing, testing, automated testing, deploying, maintaining, monitoring, and alerting.

What You'll Bring

2-5 years of hands-on software development experience in a professional setting.
Experience building full-stack applications with frameworks similar to Spring Boot, NextJS, Express, ASP.NET, Django, or Rails.
Ability to write clean, well-tested, and efficient code that passes through code review with minimal comments. Additionally, you will engage with code reviews by giving and receiving feedback to ensure high-quality outcomes.
The ability to iterate and ship ideas quickly and independently.
Self-led and motivated to proactively find answers and resolve blockers.
Experience leveraging AI tools.
Bonus: Experience using AWS services and knowledge of microservice architectures.

The displayed range represents the expected annual base salary / On-Target Earnings (OTE) for this position. On-Target Earnings (OTE) is inclusive of base salary and on-target commission earnings, which applies exclusively to sales roles.

This annual base salary forms part of a comprehensive Total Rewards Package. In addition to benefits, this role may qualify for discretionary bonuses/incentives and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Position Pay Range

€56.000—€77.000 EUR

Thoughtful perks like daily free lunch, a new car discount, meditation and fitness apps, commuting cost coverage, and more help our people create space for what matters most in their personal and professional lives.

jobs.title: AI Developer
jobs.description:
We are looking for an AI Developer to our team in Espoo or Tampere!

This permanent position is about building AI solutions that do real work in our customers' processes, and making them reliable enough to run in production. The role can be tailored according to your preferences and skills: some of our developers spend more time with the customer shaping which processes are worth automating, others go deeper into the orchestration, evaluation and operations side.

You will join a team of experienced professionals from different areas of software expertise. We work in a hybrid mode, but in this role we expect strong presence in Espoo or Tampere.

Naturally, you will have access to modern tools and strong co-operation with your colleagues.

One of our strengths in career development is our diverse range of clients and various projects in different fields. That enables us to offer versatile opportunities for our employees. At Etteplan, we are concentrating on helping our customers especially in industrial system digitalization, which means the agents you build will touch engineering data, technical documentation, service processes and industrial operations, not just chat interfaces. Many of these customers have strict requirements about where their data may go, so running models locally and on-premises is a direction we are actively building capability in.

As an AI Developer at Etteplan, the role would include (but not be limited to):

Map customer processes into agentic workflows: decide what the agent decides, what a tool does, and where a human stays in the loop
Design and build tool-using agents that plan and execute multi-step tasks, including task decomposition, state and memory handling, and controlled autonomy
Build and maintain the tool and integration layer: tool contracts and schemas, structured input and output, validation and retries, and connections to customer APIs, databases, document repositories and operational systems
Build the application around the agent, from the user-facing interface to backend services, databases, authentication and deployment pipelines
Deploy solutions where the customer needs them, whether that is Azure, another cloud, the customer's own servers, or an on-premises environment running local models
Implement the controls that make AI acceptable in an industrial context: permissions, policy checks, audit logs, and correct handling of confidential customer data
Stay up to date with the fast-moving AI tooling landscape and help us decide what is production-ready and what is not

We are looking for a person who has:

Proven experience building LLM-based applications that reached production, not only prototypes and demos
Hands-on experience with agent frameworks and orchestration, for example LangGraph, LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Semantic Kernel, Copilot Studio, n8n or equivalent
Experience working against AI and LLM APIs from several providers, including tool and function calling, structured output, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) or comparable ways of exposing tools and data to an agent
Full-stack capability: you can take a solution from user interface through backend services, databases, APIs and authentication to a running deployment
Docker and containers as part of your normal way of working, together with CI/CD and monitoring
Familiarity with cloud platforms, Azure in particular, and with AWS or Google Cloud as a plus
Ability to work directly with customers, translate ambiguous requirements into something buildable, and explain trade-offs in plain language
Working proficiency in English; Finnish is a strong advantage in customer work

We appreciate also, if you are familiar with:

Local and self-hosted inference
Efficient handling of large volumes of data
Evaluation of non-deterministic systems
Industrial context: manufacturing, energy, machinery, medical devices or defence and security, and the systems around them such as MES, PLM, ERP, IIoT or technical documentation and CCMS environments

The salary range is quite wide, reflecting our openness to both earlier‑career and more experienced professionals. What matters most to us is finding the right competencies and fit and aligning the role and compensation to match.

jobs.title: Test Engineer for SmartLink IoT Platform
jobs.description:
Your role

Connectivity is KEY! And within Atlas Copco, it has become one of the fastest-growing strategic domains. A decade of investment has given us an industry-leading fleet of more than 300,000 connected machines and 100,000 users, whose data powers SMARTLINK and drives our sales, service and operational processes worldwide. Behind it sits our IoT platform: the cloud-agnostic, event-driven backbone that ingests device telemetry, holds the model of every connected asset, and serves the portal, the mobile apps and a growing number of internal consumers. We are expanding our platform team with a Test Engineer who owns the quality of that backbone.

You are the quality owner of the platform itself, not of the screens in front of it. Your working level is services, APIs, messages and data: does a domain service behave as its contract promises, does a telemetry value survive ingestion, aggregation and retrieval unchanged, and does any of it still hold at the scale of a global fleet. You work in an agile team of developers, architects and product owners, following and sharpening our platform testing standard
so that quality is a property of how we build, not a phase at the end. The total platform team is 14 people.

Test automation here is real engineering. Our suites are written in C# on .NET
by the same standards as the product code: xUnit, Testcontainers
to spin up Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis and ClickHouse per run, .NET Aspire
to bring up the distributed application, and a shared helper library published as a NuGet package so every service team tests against the same building blocks. Suites run in Azure DevOps
pipelines per component and per environment, reporting into Xray
.

Your first months land in the middle of a platform generation change, with two generations running side by side while we migrate. It is a demanding start and the fastest way to learn the platform inside out, but it is not the whole job: the migration will finish, the platform will keep growing, and so will your scope.

In This Role, You Will

Test the platform where it lives: contract, schema and integration testing of domain services and APIs, message and event flows, and the persistence behind them.
Validate the data, not just the code: event streams, time-series and aggregated telemetry, from the message a device sends to the value the platform serves to its consumers.
Extend the shared test framework the other service teams build on, and keep those suites running as quality gates in CI/CD rather than by hand.
Solve testability as a design problem. Where a service cannot be validated on its own, work out what is needed (governed test data, stubs, simulators, contract tests, observability) and get it into the backlog before the feature is built, instead of testing on production machines.
Hold the platform to what it promises its consumers. The portal, the mobile apps and internal consumers depend on your services, so you own those contracts and work with those teams on the flows that cross the boundary.
Cover performance and load at fleet scale, through harnesses that drive the real processing pipeline rather than a simplified copy of it.
Prove migrations and domain transitions: dual-source comparison between old and new, backward compatibility per domain, and confidence at cutover.
Shape quality upstream and after the fact: turn requirements into test cases during refinement, challenge anything that cannot be verified, and triage defects across service boundaries.
Leverage AI in your daily work, and help the team keep raising the bar on how we use it.

To succeed, you will need

At Atlas Copco Group, our slogan for various positions is "hire for attitude & train for skill". We train you for these positions through on-the-job-training. Do you only partly meet the profile as outlined below? No problem! We still encourage you to apply and take this opportunity. Who knows, on-the-job-training may be available for you for this position.

Solid grounding in testing methodology, QA practice and defect analysis: functional, regression and risk-based testing.
You test services and APIs directly, not through a user interface. REST and messaging, schemas and contracts are your natural working level.
You write test code, and you write it properly: readable, reviewed, running in a CI/CD pipeline. We work in C# on .NET with xUnit; another statically typed language is fine, and we give you the room to switch.
Hands-on with SQL and comfortable judging whether data and aggregations are actually correct.
A working understanding of distributed, service-based architectures: asynchronous messaging, eventual consistency, retries and idempotency, and the ways they fail in practice.
Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis. You keep digging until you know why, not just that it failed.
Agile / Scrum experience, the confidence to say in refinement that something is not testable as specified, and fluency with AI tooling plus the judgement to verify what it produces.

In return, we offer

At Atlas Copco Group you will join an international and diverse environment with specialists from different disciplines. Our culture is rooted in Swedish values, which includes a family feeling, respect and diversity. We invest in our employees' development and well-being, and we provide a flexible work-life balance. With our inclusive and caring environment, you get the support and inspiration you need to grow. Here, your ideas are embraced, and you never stop learning.

You will have a comprehensive onboarding program, including guidance by a personal godmother/godfather. You will also have access to global job opportunities, as part of the Atlas Copco Group. We offer an interesting compensation and benefits package, including health insurance, paid leave and retirement benefits.

Job location

This role offers a hybrid working arrangement, allowing you to split your time between working remotely and being on-site at Airpower in Wilrijk, Belgium (BE).

Uniting curious minds

Behind every innovative solution, there are people working together to transform the future. With careers sparked by initiative and lifelong learning, we unite curious minds, and you could be one of them.

Grafana

PhD or Master’s degree in Control Systems, Real-Time Systems, Industrial Automation, Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Mechatronics, or a related field, combined with advanced knowledge of control architectures, industrial automation, cyber-physical systems, and systems engineering principles.
10+ years of experience in control systems, industrial automation, power systems, or other mission-critical industrial platforms.

Hands-on expertise in verification, validation, test automation, systems integration, and control system lifecycle management.
